message.content:
**Answer:** The most iconic 19th‑century sculpture is generally regarded to be **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser)** by **Auguste Rodin**, finished in 1889. **Why it’s so famous** | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin (1840–1917), a leading French sculptor who revolutionized modern sculpture. | | **Date** | 1889 – created as part of his monumental project *The Gates of Hell* (the sculpture itself was cast in 1889). | | **Medium** | Bronze (originally a plaster study). | | **Subject** | A passionate embrace between two lovers, rendered with dramatic realism and emotional intensity. | | **Cultural Impact** | • Became a symbol of romantic love and artistic freedom.
• Influenced countless artists and became a staple in art history curricula.
• Its image has been reproduced in countless prints, posters, and popular media. | | **Legacy** | • One of the first modern sculptures to capture raw human emotion rather than idealized mythological themes.
• Inspired later works such as *The Thinker* (1902) and *The Gates of Hell* (completed 1917). | **Other notable 19th‑century sculptures** - *The Gates of Hell* (Rodin, 1880–1917) – a monumental bronze relief that includes “The Kiss.” - *The Birth of Venus* (Alexandre Cabanel, 1863) – a celebrated academic painting turned into a bronze sculpture. - *The Death of Sardanapalus* (Goya, 1828) – a powerful depiction of a king’s last moments. While many masterpieces exist, “The Kiss” remains the most widely recognized and celebrated sculpture of the 19th century.
